extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners before the USPTO; disciplinary counsel; Office of Enrollment and Discipline stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for imposing reciprocal discipline by the USPTO where a practitioner has been disciplined by a state bar, including the opportunity to respond, standards for imposing identical discipline, and publication/notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline authority under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state disciplinary authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Deputy General Counsel for Enrollment and Discipline may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting identical discipline; the Director then may order reciprocal discipline (here, a public reprimand) based on the state action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and opportunity to oppose under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty days of service of the Notice and Order, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order must be served (here via certified mail). The respondent must timely assert the specific statutory/regulatory grounds listed in §11.24(d)(1) to oppose reciprocity; failure to respond affects the proceeding (see 'no genuine issue' criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible statutory reasons to oppose reciprocity (reference to 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order references these reasons but does not restate them; practitioners should consult §11.24(d)(1) directly to identify the enumerated defenses (e.g., that the disciplinary proceeding did not afford due process, that the misconduct alleged does not constitute misconduct under USPTO rules, etc.). Failure to assert these reasons timely forfeits them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and deem reciprocal discipline appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was delivered and Respondent did not file a response; accordingly the Director determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and ordered a public reprimand. Non-response thus can lead to a default factual determination supporting identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards triggering reciprocal discipline: violation of USPTO ethical rules (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed when the state disciplinary action constitutes a violation of the ethical standards set out in USPTO rules, e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states Respondent was publicly reprimanded by the USPTO for violation of §10.23(b)(6) as a result of the State Bar reprimand. Practitioners should map state-rule findings to USPTO ethical provisions to evaluate reciprocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law findings as basis for USPTO discipline (citation of Texas Disciplinary Rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary findings (here, Texas Disciplinary Rules 1.01(b)(1) and 1.03(a)) serve as the predicate for reciprocal USPTO discipline when they correspond to misconduct under USPTO rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order quotes the Texas rules: 1.01(b)(1) ('a lawyer shall not neglect a legal matter entrusted to the lawyer') and 1.03(a) ('A lawyer shall keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information'), and treats the state public reprimand as the factual basis for the USPTO reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate sanction: imposition of an identical public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is appropriate under §11.24, the Director may order the same sanction imposed by the state—here, a public reprimand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly orders that 'Respondent is publicly reprimanded' to mirror the State Bar discipline. The document shows USPTO practice of imposing identical discipline rather than imposing a different sanction in reciprocal cases absent stated grounds to the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and posting obligations (35 U.S.C. §32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.24, 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following imposition of discipline, the OED DGC shall publish the Final Order, publish a notice in the Official Gazette, and post disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room per statutory and regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires publication of the Final Order and a 'NOTICE OF REPRIMAND' in the Official Gazette and posting at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided). This demonstrates transparency obligations after discipline is imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification duty to other disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED DGC must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs that notice be given in accordance with §11.59, ensuring other jurisdictions and relevant courts are informed of the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of proper service to support proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of the Notice and Order (here by certified mail with receipt) and actual delivery to the respondent supports proceeding with reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents certified-mail service (receipt no. provided) and delivery date; properly documented service is a procedural prerequisite to triggering the respondent's forty-day response period and to later determinations when a respondent fails to respond.
